delimiter: whitespace (NOT tab -- a tab-split parse returns zero rows and reads as empty)
loader_gotcha: dna_decode.glm.genomewide.load_peak_tiles requires the 'mpra' subdir, not its parent
ceiling_rule: ceilings are PER-RUNG and must not be inherited (0.9410 belongs to the peak tiles alone); and within a rung, never quote single_replicate_agreement as the ceiling

peak_tiles.size_lever: EXHAUSTED ON THE PEAK-TILE RUNG ONLY -- 46,713 rows is the whole file and 44,106 are in use. This statement is SCOPED to peak_tiles and says nothing about any sibling rung.
peak_tiles.ceiling_field_note: ceiling_for_a_sequence_model is the Spearman-Brown step-up of single_replicate_agreement, square-rooted: the published readout is the MEAN of two replicates and is more reliable than either alone. The first version of this census reported single_replicate_agreement AS the ceiling for the fragment rungs and so understated their headroom by ~0.33.

fragments_LB.ceiling_field_note: ceiling_for_a_sequence_model is the Spearman-Brown step-up of single_replicate_agreement, square-rooted: the published readout is the MEAN of two replicates and is more reliable than either alone. The first version of this census reported single_replicate_agreement AS the ceiling for the fragment rungs and so understated their headroom by ~0.33.
fragments_LB.size_lever: UNDER-USED on this rung -- 30,000 of 321,123 rows (9.3%) is the largest N any measurement has used. DISAGREEMENT, unresolved as of 2026-10-26 -- do NOT plan work on an 'unpulled lever' premise. This field asserted "The size lever here has never been pulled." and that assertion is known-FALSE: the arm `fragment-rung-321k-rows-size-lever-LB-M9` in soraya_runs/arms-ledger.json is `measured` (resolved 2026-10-18, six days after this census was written, metric 0.185) and reports a ladder at 20k/150k with verdict DOES_NOT_GENERALISE against the pre-registered 0.05 bar. BUT its 20k/150k numbers have NO committed artifact -- the only per-run artifact is wiki/glm_genomewide_oracle_2026-10-07.json at n_train 24006 + n_test 5994 = 30,000, and the arm records that 2 of 4 planned replication runs were lost to a mid-run drive disconnect. So: the lever WAS pulled (do not re-plan it as untried), and the 150k figures are UNVERIFIABLE here (do not quote them as measured). largest_n_measured stays 30,000 because that is the largest N a committed artifact supports.

sigma70_designed.join_gap_cause: hyphen-vs-underscore in the UP-element name (gourse-326fold-up vs gourse_136fold_up); _norm_key fixes it and load_pairs enforces MIN_JOIN_RATE=0.95. NOT absent data.
sigma70_designed.factorial_note: 5-way crossed, 88.7% filled. UP_element has THREE levels, not one.
sigma70_designed.ceiling_reason: GSE108535's two published tables correlate at EXACTLY 1.0 -- one is a monotone transform of the other, not a replicate pair. No ceiling is computable, so a number on this rung has no denominator.

measured_headline.note: unlike the peak-tile rung, the crude baseline does NOT win here

sigma70_designed.size_lever: EXHAUSTED ON THE SIGMA70 RUNG ONLY -- 10,898 of 10,898 joined rows are in use under leave_element_out. Scoped to this rung. NOTE: the non-computable thing here is the CEILING (no replicate pair), which is a different limitation from the row count and must not be conflated.

corrections_2026_10_13.cause: a field present on SOME rungs and absent on others reads as a statement about ALL of them. The only size statement available said EXHAUSTED, so it was quoted as a project-level wall and 321,123 unused fragments in the same cache directory were reported as "no rows available".
corrections_2026_10_13.self_correction: the first pass of THIS amendment wrote sigma70_designed largest_n_measured=None and size_lever=NOT_COMPUTABLE claiming "no usable denominator is recorded here". That was FALSE: the rung records 10,898 rows under designed_rows, usable_joined AND n_distinct_sequences. The validator also under-reported it, because ROW_COUNT_KEYS omitted those keys -- so a missing key read as "no data" rather than "the list is incomplete". Both fixed; the error class this module targets was reproduced inside the fix for it, and is recorded rather than quietly repaired.

corrections_2026_10_26.was: The size lever here has never been pulled.
corrections_2026_10_26.now: a recorded DISAGREEMENT naming both sources; largest_n_measured unchanged at 30,000
corrections_2026_10_26.cause: this census was written 2026-10-12; the arm that pulled the lever resolved 2026-10-18 and nothing wrote back. A filename date says when a document was WRITTEN, never whether it is still TRUE. Measured consequence: a session read this field, concluded the fragment rung was the highest-value untried lever, and drafted a plan on that premise before the arm's own ledger row refuted it.
corrections_2026_10_26.why_not_resolved: the two sources cannot be reconciled from this repo. The arm's 20k/150k figures have no committed artifact (searched every wiki/*.json plus a grep for 150000/150,000/150k, 3 hits all unrelated), and the arm records 2 of 4 replication runs lost to a drive disconnect. Picking either side would assert something unverifiable.
corrections_2026_10_26.what_does_cross_check: the arm's DIRECTION, independently. This census's own best_measured_arm records kmer4 spearman 0.1313 at 30,000 rows; the arm reports kmer4 rho 0.1466 at 20,000. More rows, lower spearman -- the same direction the arm's DOES_NOT_GENERALISE verdict concluded. The verdict is corroborated; only the specific 150k numbers are not.
